# Decision needed: make the sealed primary endpoint evaluable

**Status:** proposal and offline coverage audit, **not** a ratified change to [`PREREGISTRATION.md`](PREREGISTRATION.md). No held-out model output has been inspected. Do not edit the 79-row brief manifest, its §13 seal, or the primary denominator to get a green result. Paul must ratify any §14 amendment before the first test run. The implementation in `src/eval/primary-endpoint.mjs` deliberately returns `reportable:false` until the rule plan, browser evidence verifier, and owner decision exist.

## Exact universe and the gap

The manifest seal is `sha256:89a1f47d638c5eab733074d87bc19d6615401aeb9a77ecbd86cf10b443e272b1`. It contains 79 briefs: **54 test rows**, but §6 and the existing `checkUniverse()` make only **50 generation test briefs (30 families)** the primary endpoint; **four repair test briefs (two families)** are a separate secondary endpoint. The older bead headline incorrectly treats all 54 as primary. For the 50 generation briefs, there are 237 declared routes, 165 prose journeys, 211 prose assertions, and 138 (brief, required-rule) pairs spanning 19 rule IDs. These quantities come from `auditPrimaryCoverage()` on the committed manifest; they are input obligations, **not** project pass counts.

Only 36 of 138 required-rule pairs refer to one of the six executable MWG checks in `src/corpus/rules.mjs`; 67 pairs name broad umbrella IDs (`accessibility/accessibility` **47**, `forms/forms` **14**, `html/html` **6**) that a narrower check cannot prove as a whole. Another 35 pairs name concrete rules without a check. **Zero of the 50 primary briefs** have every required rule backed by an implemented automated check. A check for `forms/required-field-feedback` does not establish `forms/forms`; likewise error announcement alone does not establish universal accessibility. `applicable_rules` may contain further guides for C2 retrieval; only the brief-fixed `required_rules` define criterion 3. A model omitting a route cannot lower any denominator.

The 165 journeys and 211 assertions are natural-language strings, not executable browser operations. `src/corpus/harness.mjs` drives a different scaffold-specific corpus; it is not a universal browser oracle for these 50 generated apps. `src/eval/endpoint.mjs` accepts `result.functional:true` and arbitrary `rule_results[rule]:true` as trusted input: that performs correct arithmetic **after** observation but does not prove a browser drove the action or a rule was checked. Passing tests with synthetic booleans must never be reported as sealed results. The blocker accessibility and security criteria also require actual coverage for labels, keyboard, focus, traps, errors, cookies, owner scope, client secrets, injection and CSRF; two hand-written zero counters are not evidence.

## Recommended decision (owner to ratify)

**Keep the 50-brief, four-arm primary estimand and the entire brief-fixed required-rule bundle.** Do not quietly replace umbrella IDs with a single easier subrule, drop difficult briefs, use a checkable-only denominator, or count an unmeasured criterion as a failure. Before opening any held-out outputs:

1. Author a versioned rule-plan keyed by *each of the 19 required IDs*. For umbrella IDs, define the concrete subproperties needed for the full umbrella, their applicability by archetype and the independent evidence path, **or** explicitly upgrade blinded dual-human ratings from the §9 sample to **every applicable primary cell** as a named deviation. A partial single check is never a full umbrella PASS. A model judge may triage but cannot certify the primary result.
2. Author a fixture-backed browser contract for *each of the 50 briefs* (237 route receipts, 165 journey receipts including persistence/reload, 211 assertion receipts), plus build/toolchain and blocker suites. Each receipt refers to a project tree/build key and a hashed browser/build artifact that the runner verifies independently. No generated code runs outside the sandbox. This work must be split into separately reviewable oracle beads rather than hiding 50 stubs in one change.
3. Freeze rule-plan SHA, runner implementation SHA, artifact format, decoded model configuration, applicability map and seal before first test. Use a dev-only dry audit to validate the pipeline. Only then may the existing `analyseSealed()` compute a 50-brief-per-arm rate and family-cluster bootstrap. If any criterion remains unobserved, status is `NOT_EVALUABLE` and **no primary percentage, CI or H1/H2 decision is published**.

The computable denominator for each arm is fixed at **50 briefs** and the planned complete design is **200 arm×brief cells**. For each required rule ID, the applicable denominator is the number of the 50 briefs that name it (e.g. accessibility umbrella 47 **per arm**), not all sites and not the number of implemented checks. Report `observed/passed/failed/unmeasured` over that fixed denominator by arm, archetype and family; a rule rate is null if any applicable receipt is missing. Repair is excluded, not discarded: report separately through the already-pinned repair endpoint. The existing §3/§4 +10pp and −5pp decision thresholds and cluster resampling by family remain unchanged.

## What the code does now, and does not do

`auditPrimaryCoverage()` counts the sealed inputs and labels currently automated vs unimplemented and umbrella rules. `evaluatePrimary()` takes externally produced per-arm receipts keyed by the **verbatim** declared route/journey/assertion/rule, refuses missing/extra entries and unplanned rules, checks evidence references have a typed hash, and reports `NOT_EVALUABLE` rather than converting instrumentation gaps to zero passes. It exposes denominators and null group pass rates whenever measurement is incomplete. Its dev-only mode exercises receipt-to-arithmetic integration with synthetic receipts and labels it `DRY_AUDIT_ONLY`; this is **not** a browser-driven acceptance run. These receipts are **not independently verified browser facts**; there is currently no ratified rule plan or artifact verifier, so even a completely populated sealed input is explicitly `AWAITING_RATIFICATION`, `reportable:false`. This is a guardrail and an implementation seam, not proof that the primary endpoint can already run. The held-out test set remains sealed and unscored.

## Next owner actions

1. Ratify, amend or reject the draft deviation; resolve whether complete umbrella proof will be automated or independently dual-rated on all applicable cells. Record this *before* outcomes, not retrospectively.
2. Assign bounded per-archetype oracle implementation and accessible/security blocker-gate work. Capture browser artifacts from dev-only examples first; no score from a route returning 200 or a mock receipt.
3. Review signed/pinned rule-plan and artifacts, then authorize the one-time held-out run through the spend gate. Until then, Gate 3 in [`READINESS-EPIC.md`](../train/READINESS-EPIC.md) is **BLOCKED**, not passed by this memo or by the dry audit.
